script:
Now turn to Part one. You will hear a man booking a swimming course at a leisure centre. First, you have some time to look at questions one to ten.
— Riverside Leisure Centre, good morning.
— Hello. I'd like to book a place on the adult swimming course.
— Of course. Can I take your name, please?
— It's Nowak. That's N, O, W, A, K.
— Nowak. Thank you. And a contact number?
— It's oh-seven-two-two, three-one-five, eight-double-four.
— Let me read that back. Oh-seven-two-two, three-one-five, eight-double-four.
— That's right.
— Now, we run two adult courses. There's Improvers on Tuesdays and Beginners on Thursdays.
— I can swim a little, but not very far. Maybe twenty metres.
— Then Improvers would be too fast. I'd put you in the Thursday class.
— Thursday is fine. What time does it start?
— Half past seven in the evening, and it runs for fifty minutes.
— And how many weeks is the course?
— It's eight weeks. It began last month, but you can join now and we'll carry the missed sessions over to the next one.
— That's helpful. What does it cost?
— The full course is ninety pounds. Because you're joining late, you'd pay sixty-five.
— Sixty-five. Do I pay today?
— You can pay on your first evening, at reception. We take cards, but not cash.
— Fine. Is there anything I need to bring?
— A towel and a swimming cap. Caps are compulsory in all our pools. You can buy one here for four pounds if you forget.
— And where do I go when I arrive?
— The changing rooms are on the lower floor. The teacher meets the class at the shallow end.
— Does the class ever get cancelled?
— Only if the pool has to close, and we send a text the same morning if that happens. The missed week is added to the end of the course.
— One more thing. Is there parking?
— There is, but it's free for two hours only. After that it's three pounds. Most of our evening students park on Mill Street instead, which is free after six.
— I'll do that. Thank you very much.
— You're welcome. We'll see you on Thursday.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — surname:
items.rationale: The name is spelt out letter by letter, which is the point of the item: a candidate writing from the sound alone produces Novak.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — class day:
items.rationale: Two days are named and Tuesday is ruled out because the caller can only swim a short distance, so the day must be taken from the recommendation and not from the first mention.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — start time:
items.rationale: The time is given once, in words, and the length of the lesson follows immediately, so a candidate who writes the first number heard may record the fifty minutes instead.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — length of each lesson:
items.rationale: Said in the same breath as the start time, which is what makes the pair of items work.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — number of weeks:
items.rationale: The course length is stated plainly, immediately before the explanation about joining late, which is the distraction.

items.stem: How much will the man pay?
items.rationale: Ninety is the full price and sixty-five is what he pays because he is joining late; both figures are said in consecutive sentences.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — where payment is made:
items.prompt: Pay at ___ on the first evening
items.rationale: The place is named once and is followed by the method of payment, which is the more prominent detail.

items.stem: What must every swimmer wear?
items.rationale: Two things are to be brought and only one of them is compulsory, which the clerk states directly.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — where the changing rooms are:
items.rationale: The floor and the meeting point are given together, so a candidate must hold two locations apart.

items.stem: Swimming course booking — where evening students park:
items.rationale: The centre's own parking is described first and is only partly free, so the answer is the alternative named afterwards.

script:
Now turn to Part one. You will hear a woman returning a faulty kettle to a shop. First, you have some time to look at questions one to ten.
— Customer service, good morning.
— Hello. I bought a kettle here and it has stopped heating.
— I'm sorry to hear that. When did you buy it?
— Three weeks ago, on the twelfth.
— Do you have the receipt?
— I have the email one on my phone.
— That's fine, an email receipt is accepted. Can I take your name?
— It's Adeyemi. A, D, E, Y, E, M, I.
— Adeyemi. Thank you. Which kettle was it?
— The Brantwood, the white one. It was thirty-four pounds.
— And what exactly is wrong?
— It switches on, the light comes on, but the water never gets hot.
— Right. Within thirty days you may choose a refund or an exchange. After thirty days it goes for repair first.
— I'd rather have a different model. The same one might do the same thing.
— Then an exchange. The Brantwood is thirty-four and the next model up, the Halden, is forty-one, so there would be seven pounds to pay.
— That's fine.
— Have you brought the box?
— No, I threw it away. Is that a problem?
— Not for an exchange. It only matters for a refund, where we need the packaging.
— Good. How long will it take?
— Five minutes at the desk, but the Halden is not on the shelf today. It comes in on Thursday.
— Can you hold one for me?
— I can, for forty-eight hours. Come to the collection point at the back of the store, not this desk.
— Will the guarantee start again on the new one?
— It will. A replacement carries a fresh two-year guarantee from the day you collect it, and we register that for you at the counter.
— That's good to know.
— Do I bring the old kettle?
— Please. We can't complete the exchange without it, and bring the charger cable as well if it is separate.
— It isn't, it's attached. Thank you very much.
— You're welcome. We'll see you on Thursday.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — surname:
items.rationale: Spelt out on request, which is the only reliable way for a candidate to record an unfamiliar name.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — date of purchase:
items.rationale: The date is given after the period, so a candidate who writes the first number heard records the three weeks instead.

items.stem: What proof of purchase does the shop accept?
items.rationale: The customer offers the email version and the assistant confirms it is accepted, which is the point being tested.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — make of the faulty kettle:
items.rationale: Two product names are used in the conversation and only one is the faulty item.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — price of the faulty kettle:
items.rationale: Three sums appear in quick succession and only the first is what she paid.

items.stem: What is wrong with the kettle?
items.rationale: The description contains two things that do work and one that does not, and the question asks for the fault.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — extra amount to pay:
items.rationale: The difference is stated after the two prices, so a candidate may write one of the prices instead.

items.stem: Why does the missing box not matter?
options: It is only needed for a refund
The shop supplies a new box
items.rationale: The assistant draws the distinction explicitly between an exchange and a refund.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — when the new model arrives:
items.rationale: The day is given once and repeated at the end of the call.

items.stem: Kettle exchange — where to collect:
items.prompt: Go to the collection point at the ___ of the store
items.rationale: The assistant names the place and then rules out the desk they are standing at.

Now turn to Part one. You will hear a man joining a public library. First, you have some time to look at questions one to ten.
— Good afternoon. I'd like to join the library.
— Certainly. Have you lived in the city long?
— About six weeks. I moved here for work.
— That's fine. I'll need your name and an address.
— My name is Ferreira. F, E, double R, E, I, R, A.
— Ferreira. And the address?
— Flat nine, Ashcroft House, Weston Road.
— Flat nine, Ashcroft House. Do you have anything with that address on it? A bank letter or a bill?
— I have a phone bill on my phone. Is that all right?
— A photograph of one isn't accepted, I'm afraid. It has to be a paper copy, or a letter. A driving licence would do as well.
— I can bring a bank letter tomorrow.
— That's fine. I'll start the card now and you can activate it when you come back. Now, some details about borrowing. You may take out twelve items at a time.
— Twelve. And for how long?
— Books are three weeks, and you can renew twice. DVDs are one week and cannot be renewed at all.
— Are there any charges?
— Borrowing is free. There's a fine of ten pence a day on a late book, up to a maximum of five pounds.
— And if I lose something?
— Then you pay what it costs to replace it, plus a three-pound administration charge.
— I understand. Do you have computers?
— We do, on the first floor. Members get one hour a day free, and you book it at the desk upstairs, not here.
— Is there anything on at the weekend? I have children.
— There's a story session for under-fives every Saturday at eleven. It's popular, so come a few minutes early. There's also a homework club on Sundays, but that's for secondary pupils.
— And can I return books to any branch?
— To any of the five branches, yes, and there is a returns box outside this one for when we are closed.
— Thank you. That's very helpful.

items.stem: Library membership — surname:
items.rationale: Spelt out with a double letter, which is what the item tests.

items.stem: Library membership — flat number:
items.rationale: The number is given inside a longer address and repeated by the clerk, so it can be confirmed on a second hearing.

items.stem: What proof of address will be accepted?
items.rationale: The photograph is explicitly refused and three acceptable forms are named, one of which the man says he will bring.

items.stem: Library membership — number of items borrowed at once:
items.rationale: The number is repeated by the member, which is the confirmation the item relies on.

items.stem: Library membership — loan period for books:
items.rationale: Two loan periods are given in the same sentence, one for books and one for DVDs.

items.stem: Library membership — daily fine on a late book:
items.rationale: The fine and its maximum are said together, so the candidate must take the smaller number.

items.stem: Library membership — maximum fine:
items.rationale: The pair of numbers is the point: one is in pence a day and the other is a ceiling in pounds.

items.stem: Library membership — extra charge for a lost item:
items.rationale: The replacement cost is variable and the administration charge is fixed, and only the fixed one can be written down.

items.stem: Where are computer sessions booked?
items.rationale: The clerk says explicitly that booking is upstairs and not at the desk where the conversation is taking place.

items.stem: Library membership — time of the Saturday story session:
items.rationale: Two weekend activities are described and only one has a time, and the other is for a different age group.

script:
Now turn to Part one. You will hear a woman arranging a repair to a washing machine. First, you have some time to look at questions one to ten.
— Appliance repairs, good morning.
— Hello. My washing machine has stopped working and I'd like someone to look at it.
— I can arrange that. Can I take your name?
— It's Osei. O, S, E, I.
— Thank you. And the make of the machine?
— It's a Voller. I bought it about four years ago.
— Do you know the model?
— There's a number on the door. It says W, D, six-one-five-oh.
— WD six-one-five-oh. What's the machine doing?
— It fills with water and then stops. The drum doesn't turn at all.
— And is there a light or a code showing?
— Yes, there's an E and then the number four.
— E-four usually means the motor, though it can be the belt. Either way the engineer will need to open it, so I'll book a full visit rather than a check.
— How much is that?
— The visit is fifty-five pounds, which includes the first half hour. Parts are extra. If it is the belt, the part is about twenty pounds; a motor is nearer a hundred and forty.
— And when could someone come?
— I have Wednesday morning or Friday afternoon this week.
— Wednesday would be better.
— Then I'll put you down for Wednesday, between eight and twelve. The engineer will ring about half an hour before.
— Will I need to do anything before he arrives?
— Please pull the machine out from the wall if you can, and empty the drum. If there's water in it, put a towel underneath.
— The drum is full of water now. How do I empty it?
— There's a small filter behind a flap at the bottom. Open it slowly with a bowl underneath. If you'd rather not, the engineer will do it, but it adds about twenty minutes.
— I'll try. And how do I pay?
— By card, to the engineer, on the day. We don't take cash and we don't invoice.

items.stem: Repair booking — surname:
items.rationale: Short and spelt out, which is the only reliable way to record it.

items.stem: Repair booking — make of machine:
items.rationale: The make is given once and the age of the machine follows, which is the distraction.

items.stem: Repair booking — model number:
items.rationale: Read as separate digits and repeated back, so a candidate has two chances and must write digits rather than words.

items.stem: What is the machine doing?
items.rationale: The fault is described in two clauses and the second is the one that matters.

items.stem: Repair booking — error code shown:
items.rationale: Given as a letter and a number spoken separately, which is what the item tests.

items.stem: Repair booking — cost of the visit:
items.rationale: Three sums are given in quick succession and only the first is the visit itself.

items.stem: When will the engineer come?
items.rationale: Two slots are offered and the customer chooses one, so the answer is her reply rather than the first option named.

items.stem: Repair booking — how long before arrival the engineer telephones:
items.rationale: Expressed as half an hour rather than as a number, so a candidate must convert it.

items.stem: Repair booking — what to put under the machine:
items.rationale: Two preparations are asked for and only one applies when there is water in the drum.

items.stem: How must the customer pay?
items.rationale: The clerk names the method and then rules out the two alternatives explicitly.
